figures.shows: A top view of a listener that faces minus Z with plus X on its right and a source on the right, then the same listener turned to face plus Z, where the source is on the left
figures.caption: The right side is always forward crossed with up, so turning the listener round swaps the ears of a source.
figures.alt: Two panels seen from above. In the left panel a listener faces up the page along minus Z, plus X points right and a source on the right is marked louder in the right ear. In the right panel the listener faces down the page along plus Z, its right side is minus X and the same source is on its left.

figures.shows: The gain against distance for the four attenuation models with minimum distance 1, maximum distance 50 and rolloff 1, with the clamped regions shaded
figures.caption: Inverse and exponential coincide, linear reaches silence at the maximum distance, and nothing changes in the shaded regions.
figures.alt: A line chart of gain from 0 to 1 against distance from 0 to 60. A flat line stays at 1. The inverse and exponential curve falls fast to 0.02 at 50. A straight line falls to 0 at 50. Both ends of the distance axis are shaded as clamped.
